title: Colombia Digital Nomad Visa (Visa V Nómadas Digitales): Complete 2026 Guide
author: María Fernanda Duarte
excerpt: Everything remote workers and tech entrepreneurs need to know about requirements, minimum income, bank statements, and avoiding common rejection mistakes in Colombia.
content:
## Introduction to the Colombian Digital Nomad Visa

Colombia remains one of the premier global destinations for remote professionals, entrepreneurs, and digital creatives. The **Visa V Nómadas Digitales** allows foreigners who work remotely for overseas employers or manage their own foreign-incorporated businesses to reside legally in Colombia for up to two years.

In this comprehensive guide, our immigration team breaks down the legal prerequisites, documentary thresholds, and practical tips to ensure your application gets approved smoothly.

---

## Core Eligibility Requirements

To qualify under Resolution 5477, applicants must satisfy three essential pillars:

1. **Remote Work Employment or Ownership**: Proof that you provide remote services exclusively for companies incorporated outside of Colombia, or own/operate a foreign enterprise.
2. **Financial Solvency (Income Threshold)**: Bank account statements demonstrating an average monthly income equivalent to at least **three (3) Colombian Minimum Monthly Legal Wages (SMLMV)** over the last 3 months.
3. **Health & Medical Coverage**: Comprehensive international health insurance covering medical expenses, accidents, and repatriation within Colombian territory with a policy validity matching the visa duration.

> **Key Legal Note**: This visa does not authorize you to work for or receive local payroll salary from Colombian entities. Local Colombian employment requires a different visa category (Visa M Trabajador).

---

## Document Checklist

Make sure to prepare all materials in advance, officially translated into Spanish if issued in another language:

- Valid passport with at least 6 months before expiration and minimum 2 blank pages.
- Letter of employment written in Spanish (or officially translated) stating remote work arrangement, role, and salary.
- Certified bank statements demonstrating the monthly minimum wage threshold.
- International health insurance certificate explicitly mentioning Colombia coverage.
- Clear motivational letter detailing your planned activities and intended base city (e.g., Medellín, Bogotá, Cartagena).

---

## Why Applications Get Delayed or Denied

The most frequent grounds for observation (Requerimiento) or refusal include:

- Inconsistent account statements with unexplained capital injections.
- Insurance policies that exclude sports, emergency evacuation, or repatriation.
- Missing official certified translations for bank documents.

If you need tailored guidance on gathering documents, schedule an assessment with our bilingual immigration attorneys today.

title: Buying Real Estate in Medellín: Essential Due Diligence for Foreign Investors
author: María Fernanda Duarte
excerpt: A step-by-step legal blueprint to purchasing residential or commercial property in Colombia safely, registering titles, and structuring foreign exchange transactions.
content:
## Buying Property in Colombia as a Foreigner

Investing in Medellín real estate (especially in zones like El Poblado, Laureles, and Envigado) provides solid appreciation and attractive rental returns. However, the legal transaction workflow in Colombia is fundamentally different from Anglo-Saxon title-escrow practices.

Foreign buyers have the exact same rights to own real estate as Colombian citizens, but navigating title verification and legal clearance is vital to prevent hidden liens or ownership conflicts.

---

## The Due Diligence Checklist (Estudio de Títulos)

Before signing any promise of sale (*Promesa de Compraventa*) or transferring earnest money, our firm conducts a 10 to 20-year title audit covering:

1. **Certificado de Tradición y Libertad**: Current chain of title, confirming no legal mortgages, embargoes, judicial lawsuits, or heritage freezes.
2. **Paz y Salvo de Predial & Valorización**: Municipal certificates ensuring the property has zero pending tax debts or road infrastructure assessments.
3. **Property Management Clearance**: Certificado de Paz y Salvo de Administración from the horizontal property building council.
4. **Public Deed Verification**: Examining the original *Escritura Pública* at the public notary (*Notaría*) to identify easements, reserve rights, or family patrimony encumbrances.

---

## Central Bank Registration (Formulario 4)

All funds brought into Colombia for direct real estate investment must be declared through the **Banco de la República (Central Bank)** via international exchange forms.

Doing this correctly ensures two crucial legal advantages:
- Clean repatriation of capital and dividends when selling in the future.
- Potential qualification for the **Visa M Inversionista Inmobiliario** (Real Estate Investor Visa) if your purchase surpasses the legal minimum SMLMV threshold.

title: Forming a SAS (Simplified Stock Corporation) in Colombia: A Practical Guide
author: Capital M Law Team
excerpt: Why the SAS vehicle is the gold standard for international entrepreneurs entering Colombia, covering bylaws, tax IDs (RUT), and corporate bank accounts.
content:
## Why Choose a SAS Company?

The **Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (SAS)**, created under Law 1258 of 2008, revolutionized corporate law in Colombia. It is by far the most agile and flexible corporate structure for foreign entrepreneurs and investors.

### Key Advantages
- **Single Shareholder Allowed**: You can incorporate with 100% foreign ownership and just one natural person or corporate shareholder.
- **Limited Liability**: Shareholders are exclusively responsible up to their subscribed capital contributions.
- **Flexible Bylaws**: Great liberty in structuring voting rights, share classes, dividend distributions, and board provisions.

---

## Incorporation Steps

1. **Drafting Corporate Bylaws**: Tailored estatutos defining registered business address, commercial purpose, legal representation, and powers.
2. **Chamber of Commerce Registration**: Filing at the *Cámara de Comercio de Medellín para Antioquia* to obtain the legal Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation.
3. **Tax Identification (RUT - DIAN)**: Obtaining the corporate tax ID from the national tax and customs authority.
4. **Opening Corporate Bank Account**: Submitting beneficial ownership documentation to comply with SAGRILAFT and anti-money laundering regulations.

title: Tax Residency in Colombia: 183-Day Rule and Global Income Impact
author: Legal Research Desk
excerpt: A clear explanation of when an expat becomes a Colombian tax resident and how worldwide assets and income are assessed by DIAN.
content:
## When Do You Become a Tax Resident in Colombia?

Under Article 10 of the Colombian Tax Statute (*Estatuto Tributario*), an individual becomes a tax resident in Colombia if they stay in the country—continuously or discontinuously—for **more than 183 calendar days** within any 365-consecutive-day period.

### Consequences of Tax Residency
- **Worldwide Income Reporting**: Tax residents must declare income earned both inside and outside Colombia to DIAN.
- **Asset Declarations**: Obligation to file the annual report of foreign assets (*Declaración de Activos en el Exterior*) if your assets surpass the minimum UVT threshold.
- **Tax Treaties**: Colombia has double taxation avoidance treaties (CDI) with countries such as Spain, Canada, the UK, Switzerland, France, and others, helping prevent double assessment.

title: 5 Vital Clauses Every Colombian Lease Agreement Must Include
author: María Fernanda Duarte
excerpt: Protecting tenants and landlords alike: lease renewals, deposit laws under Ley 820, repair obligations, and early termination penalties.
content:
## Residential Leases Under Colombian Law 820 of 2003

Residential renting in Colombia is strictly governed by **Law 820 of 2003**. Many foreigners rent without realizing that standard lease templates downloaded online often contain legally unenforceable clauses.

### 1. Prohibition of Security Deposits for Residential Leases
Under Article 16 of Law 820, landlords are strictly prohibited from demanding cash security deposits (*depósitos en efectivo*) for residential contracts. Guarantees must be structured through insurance policies (*pólizas de arrendamiento*) or co-signers (*codeudor*).

### 2. Automatic Renewal Notice Rules
Leases renew automatically under the same terms unless either party gives written notice via certified post at least 3 months prior to expiration.

### 3. Clear Demarcation of Repairs
Locative repairs caused by everyday wear are tenant obligations, while structural and necessary repairs (water leaks, roofing, pipe failures) remain the exclusive duty of the owner.

### 4. Early Termination Penalties
Tenants can legally terminate early by giving 3 months' advance written notice and paying an indemnity equal to 3 months of rent.

title: Transitioning from Migrant (M) Visa to Permanent Resident (R) Visa
author: María Fernanda Duarte
excerpt: The roadmap from holding a 2 to 5-year Migrant Visa to permanent Colombian residency, continuous stay calculations, and citizenship paths.
content:
## Moving Towards Permanent Residency in Colombia

Holding a Migrant (M) visa is often the foundation for foreign nationals wishing to plant long-term roots in Colombia. Under current immigration regulations, individuals who hold certain types of M visas continuously can apply for the **Visa R (Residente)**.

### Time Accumulation Requirements
- **Marriage / Companion Visa (M Cónyuge / Compañero)**: Requires 3 continuous years holding the M visa.
- **Investor Visa (M Inversionista)**: Requires 5 continuous years.
- **Pensioner Visa (M Pensionado)**: Requires 5 continuous years.
- **Worker Visa (M Trabajador)**: Requires 5 continuous years.

### Continuous Stay Rule
You cannot be outside of Colombia for more than 180 continuous days during the qualifying holding period, or the residency clock resets.

Consult with our legal department to audit your entry and exit stamps before initiating your Visa R petition.
